site.title: Ankole
site.description: Ankole is a self-hosted AgentOS for shared AI colleagues. One installation, many agents, real responsibilities — on infrastructure you control.
hero.title: The AgentOS for shared AI colleagues
hero.subtitle: One installation, many agents, real responsibilities — on infrastructure you control. Ankole moves AI work out of the private chat box and into the places where work already happens.
hero.stack.label: Runs on
quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.subtitle: Run from source or deploy with Docker Compose or Helm.
quickstart.source.note: Prepare the toolchains through the repository installer, then start the complete development environment with bun dev.
quickstart.docker.note: Deploy the single-host production stack with PostgreSQL, one Worker, and Caddy HTTPS.
quickstart.k8s.body: The public Helm chart deploys the verified image pair, shared Agent Home storage, and bundled or external PostgreSQL.
differentiators.title: How Ankole is different
differentiators.subtitle: Five properties that separate Ankole from a private chat box.
differentiators.shared.title: Shared by default, not private chat
differentiators.shared.body: Agents join team-visible channels and provider contexts; multiple humans can observe, steer, and continue the same work.
differentiators.identity.title: Durable identity, not a prompt convention
differentiators.identity.body: Humans and agents are Principals with permission grants and audit trails, so authorization is a runtime concern.
differentiators.sessions.title: Long-running actor sessions, not request/response
differentiators.sessions.body: Sessions wake, receive signals, checkpoint, stream progress, hibernate, and recover with context.
differentiators.context.title: Operator-owned context, not vendor-hosted
differentiators.context.body: Memory, configuration, credentials, and audit live in your infrastructure on a self-hosted installation.
differentiators.control.title: Live control plus durable truth
differentiators.control.body: ZeroMQ RuntimeFabric carries live actor, worker, and RPC traffic while PostgreSQL remains the source of replay, fences, and final commits.
features.title: What Ankole adds
features.subtitle: One installation covers the whole surface of shared AI work.
features.sources.title: Many sources
features.sources.body: IM, webhooks, scheduled reminders, internal systems, and future provider adapters all become normalized signal input.
features.agents.title: Many agents
features.agents.body: One installation hosts multiple agents with different missions, access, tools, memory, and outbound identities.
features.sessions.title: Session actors
features.sessions.body: The long-running execution unit is actor_id = '{agent_id, session_id}' — where context, workspace state, steering, cancellation, and recovery meet.
features.context.title: Owned context
features.context.body: Conversations, model turns, summaries, signal projections, decisions, and corrections live in your infrastructure.
features.control.title: Operator control
features.control.body: Access, configuration, Agent Library defaults, plugin activation, actor leases, outbox side effects, and audit surfaces belong to the installation operator.
features.computer.title: Agent Computer
features.computer.body: The LLM loop, tools, files, terminal state, and streaming output run inside a Bun + TypeScript computer close to the workspace.
usecases.title: Work that needs an owner, not just an answer
usecases.subtitle: Ankole should make these workflows natural.
usecases.coding.title: Coding agent
usecases.coding.body: Watches an issue, reproduces the bug, changes code, opens a draft PR, and reports what still needs a human decision.
usecases.customerSuccess.title: Customer-success agent
usecases.customerSuccess.body: Observes a shared group chat, records the important facts, updates work state, and escalates privately only when needed.
usecases.research.title: Research agent
usecases.research.body: Monitors markets, policy, competitors, and internal notes, then follows up when a change matters.
usecases.qa.title: QA agent
usecases.qa.body: Works through a test backlog, gathers evidence, and hands off failures with enough context for review.
usecases.operations.title: Operations agent
usecases.operations.body: Watches alerts, prepares a runbook, and asks for approval before taking risky action.
usecases.quote: “Hold this seat, use the available context, and be judged by the result.”
bets.title: Built on five technical bets
bets.subtitle: Actor model for long-lived work identity, OTP for failure semantics, ZeroMQ for live activation, Agent Computer for local execution, PostgreSQL for durable truth.
bets.actors.title: Virtual Actors for AI work
bets.actors.body: A session is a stateful work identity with an address, mailbox, lifecycle, and recovery path — not loose background work.
bets.otp.title: OTP supervision trees as failure domains
bets.otp.body: If one agent hangs, times out, or crashes, Ankole can isolate or restart that branch without turning it into a deployment-wide failure.
bets.fabric.title: ZeroMQ activation fabric for live control
bets.fabric.body: Wakeups, steering, checkpoints, streaming, and backpressure move through a low-latency routing layer while the agent is still working.
bets.computer.title: Agent Computer as the execution substrate
bets.computer.body: The LLM loop, tools, files, terminal state, and streaming output run inside a Bun + TypeScript computer close to the workspace.
bets.ledger.title: Durable Ledger for recovery and audit
bets.ledger.body: Mailboxes, turns, reminders, decisions, and committed side effects outlive processes. Streaming is progress; committed work is truth.
cta.title: Run your own AI colleagues
cta.body: Ankole is Apache-2.0 open source and self-hosted. Deploy it on your infrastructure and keep your context.
